title: "Cell options"
format:
  html:

filters:
  - path: ../../_filters/show-source.lua
    at: pre-ast
  - panzoom
panzoom:
  loop: true
---

Keeping an image or a cell out of panzoom, and setting options on one cell. The
YAML header sets `loop`, so the gallery in [case 7](#c7) wraps around. lightbox
is off, so clicking an image panzoom leaves alone does nothing.

```yaml
---
filters:
  - panzoom
panzoom:
  loop: true
---
```

The `caption` and `description` options are on [captions and
descriptions](g-captions.html), and `fit` is on [wide and tall
figures](h-wide.html).

The plots are drawn with this helper:

```{r}
wave <- function(k = 1) {
  x <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 400)
  col <- hcl.colors(4, "Dark 3")[k]
  plot(
    x,
    sin(k * x),
    type = "n",
    main = paste("Wave", k),
    xlab = "x",
    ylab = "sin(kx)"
  )
  polygon(
    c(x, rev(x)),
    c(sin(k * x), rep(0, length(x))),
    col = adjustcolor(col, 0.35),
    border = NA
  )
  lines(x, sin(k * x), lwd = 2, col = col)
}
```

## Opt out an image {#c1 expect-open="nothing panzoom"}

Two images in a `.panzoom` div, which marks every image inside it. The first has
`.nopanzoom`, which keeps it out, so clicking it does nothing. The second opens
in panzoom.

```markdown {.show-source}
::: {.panzoom layout-ncol="2"}
![Waves breaking below the clay cliffs at Aquinnah, Martha's Vineyard.](../../images/mv-1.jpg){.nopanzoom fig-alt="Waves breaking below grassy clay cliffs at Aquinnah"}

![Edgartown Lighthouse, Martha's Vineyard.](../../images/mv-2.jpg){fig-alt="A white lighthouse against a blue sky"}
:::
```

## Opt out a cell {#c2 expect-open="nothing"}

An R cell with `#| panzoom: false` inside a `.panzoom` div. The cell option wins
over the div, so clicking the plot does nothing.

````markdown {.code-overflow-wrap .cell-code}
::: {.panzoom}
```{{r}}
#| panzoom: false
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 1: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| fig-cap: "Wave 1: y = sin(x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 1)
```
:::
````

::: {.panzoom}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| panzoom: false
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 1: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| fig-cap: "Wave 1: y = sin(x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 1)
```
:::

## No hint {#c3 expect-open="panzoom" expect-hint="hidden" expect-hint-key="nothing"}

An R cell with `hint: false` under the `panzoom` cell option. It opens in
panzoom without the hint line, which the page shows by default, and the h key
does nothing.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 3: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| panzoom:
#|   hint: false
#| fig-cap: "Wave 3: y = sin(3x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 3)
```

## Default hint {#c4 expect-open="panzoom" expect-hint="shown"}

An R cell with no hint option. It opens in panzoom with the hint line at the
bottom, except when opened by a tap.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 4: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: "Wave 4: y = sin(4x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 4)
```

## Zoom limit {#c5 expect-open="panzoom" expect-max-zoom="2"}

An R cell with `max-zoom: 2` under the `panzoom` cell option. It opens in
panzoom, and zooming in stops at 2 screen pixels per image pixel.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 1: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| panzoom:
#|   max-zoom: 2
#| fig-cap: "Wave 1: y = sin(x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 1)
```

## Options on a cell in a `.panzoom` div {#c6 expect-open="panzoom" expect-hint="hidden" expect-max-zoom="2"}

An R cell with `max-zoom: 2` and `hint: false` under the `panzoom` cell option,
inside a `.panzoom` div. The cell's options apply as they do outside the div: it
opens in panzoom without the hint line, and zooming in stops at 2 screen pixels
per image pixel.

````markdown {.code-overflow-wrap .cell-code}
::: {.panzoom}
```{{r}}
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 2: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| panzoom:
#|   max-zoom: 2
#|   hint: false
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 2: y = sin(2x), its area to the axis shaded.

wave(k = 2)
```
:::
````

::: {.panzoom}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 2: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| panzoom:
#|   max-zoom: 2
#|   hint: false
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 2: y = sin(2x), its area to the axis shaded.

wave(k = 2)
```
:::

## Looping gallery {#c7 expect-open="panzoom"}

One R cell with three plots, joined by `group: waves` under the `panzoom` cell
option. Each opens in panzoom, in a three-image gallery. The YAML header sets
`loop: true` under the `panzoom:` option, so the gallery wraps around: on wave
one, the left arrow key or the previous button goes to wave three, and on wave
three, the right arrow key or the next button goes back to wave one.

```{r}
#| fig-alt:
#|   - >-
#|     Plot titled Wave 1: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded
#|   - >-
#|     Plot titled Wave 2: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded
#|   - >-
#|     Plot titled Wave 3: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded
#| panzoom:
#|   group: waves
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "Wave 1: y = sin(x), its area to the axis shaded."
#|   - "Wave 2: y = sin(2x), its area to the axis shaded."
#|   - "Wave 3: y = sin(3x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 1)
wave(k = 2)
wave(k = 3)
```

## No alt text {#c8 expect-open="panzoom" expect-caption="none"}

An image with `.panzoom` and no alt text. It opens in panzoom with no caption,
and the link around it is labeled "Open image" for screen readers. With no
caption it isn't a figure, so it sits at the left like any image in a paragraph.

```markdown {.show-source}
![](../../images/mv-4.jpg){.panzoom width=40%}
```

## Caption beside the image {#c9 expect-open="panzoom" expect-desc-position="right"}

An R cell with `desc-position: right` and a description under the `panzoom` cell
option. It opens in panzoom, with the caption and description in a panel on the
right of the image.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 2: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| panzoom:
#|   desc-position: right
#|   description: "The area between the curve and the axis is shaded."
#| fig-cap: "Wave 2: y = sin(2x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 2)
```

## Caption above the image {#c10 expect-open="panzoom" expect-desc-position="top"}

An R cell with `desc-position: top` under the `panzoom` cell option. It opens in
panzoom, with the caption above the image.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 3: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| panzoom:
#|   desc-position: top
#| fig-cap: "Wave 3: y = sin(3x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 3)
```

## Plots held to the end of a cell {#c11 expect-open="panzoom" expect-steps="true"}

An R cell with `fig-show: hold` and `group: held` under the `panzoom` cell
option, printing text between its two plots. The text comes first on the page
and the plots after it. They open in panzoom as a two-image gallery, each with
its own caption.

```{r}
#| fig-alt:
#|   - >-
#|     Plot titled Wave 1: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded
#|   - >-
#|     Plot titled Wave 2: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded
#| fig-show: hold
#| panzoom:
#|   group: held
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "Wave 1: y = sin(x), its area to the axis shaded."
#|   - "Wave 2: y = sin(2x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 1)
print("Printed between the two plots.")
wave(k = 2)
```

## Hint starts hidden {#c12 expect-open="panzoom" expect-hint="hidden" expect-hint-key="shows"}

An R cell with `hint: hide` under the `panzoom` cell option. It opens in panzoom
without the hint line, and the h key shows it.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 4: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| panzoom:
#|   hint: hide
#| fig-cap: "Wave 4: y = sin(4x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 4)
```

## Gallery with the caption on the right {#c13 expect-open="panzoom" expect-desc-position="right" expect-steps="true"}

One R cell with three plots, joined by `group: right-waves` and set to
`desc-position: right` under the `panzoom` cell option. Each opens in panzoom,
in a three-image gallery, with its caption in a panel on the right of the image.
The captions differ in length, so the panel changes width from one image to the
next, and the image refits beside it.

```{r}
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Plot titled Wave 1: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#|   - "Plot titled Wave 2: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#|   - "Plot titled Wave 3: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| panzoom:
#|   group: right-waves
#|   desc-position: right
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "Wave 1: y = sin(x)."
#|   - "Wave 2: y = sin(2x), its area to the axis shaded."
#|   - >-
#|     Wave 3: y = sin(3x), its area to the axis shaded, with three full
#|     periods across the plot.

wave(k = 1)
wave(k = 2)
wave(k = 3)
```

## Gallery with mixed caption positions {#c14 expect-open="panzoom" expect-desc-position="right; top; bottom" expect-steps="true"}

Three R cells joined by `group: sides` under the `panzoom` cell option: the
first with `desc-position: right`, the second with `desc-position: top`, and the
third with neither. They open in panzoom as a three-image gallery, with the
caption on the right, above, and below in turn; stepping between them moves the
caption and refits the image.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 4: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| panzoom:
#|   group: sides
#|   desc-position: right
#| fig-cap: "Wave 4: y = sin(4x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 4)
```

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 5: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| panzoom:
#|   group: sides
#|   desc-position: top
#| fig-cap: "Wave 5: y = sin(5x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 5)
```

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Plot titled Wave 6: a sine curve with its area to the axis shaded"
#| panzoom:
#|   group: sides
#| fig-cap: "Wave 6: y = sin(6x), its area to the axis shaded."

wave(k = 6)
```
